verses.12:3: {uq3} o meu inimigo {exaltabitur} sobre mim? * {respice}, e escutai-me, Senhor, meu Deus.
verses.12:4b: Iluminai os meus olhos, para que eu nunca {obdormiam} na morte: * para que não diga o meu inimigo: Prevaleci contra ele.
verses.12:5b: Os que me atribulam exultarão, {motus}: * mas eu esperei na vossa misericórdia.
verses.12:6b: O meu coração exultará na vossa salvação: † cantarei ao Senhor, {tribuit}: * {psallam}.

decisions.why: The psalm opens with four questions of ‘how long’: úsquequo three times (ἕως πότε) and once quámdiu (ἕως τίνος). Glossary: úsquequo → até quando (working; Ps 4:3, 6:4). The Latin varies the third; the Greek varies it too, but the two Greek phrases mean the same (‘until when / until what time’), so by D15’s test the variation is an elegance and Portuguese may say ‘até quando’ four times. quámdiu has two other places, both ‘as long as I live’ (103:33 quámdiu sum, 145:2a quámdiu fúero), which are another use and will be ‘enquanto’. Douay-Rheims ‘How long’ ×4; Matos Soares 1932 ‘Até quando’ ×4.

options.label: Até quando ×4
options.note: Ruling: the glossary’s phrase four times, the anaphora of the lament heard as one cry (Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932).

options.label: Até quando ×3, Por quanto tempo
options.note: The Latin’s variation kept at 12:2. Two syllables longer, and it breaks the run.

decisions.why: in finem (εἰς τέλος): ‘to the end, utterly, for ever’; 19 verses (grep), several in the same frame (78:5 Úsquequo, Dómine, irascéris in finem; 88:47 Úsquequo, Dómine, avértis in finem; 73:19 ne obliviscáris in finem). The Ps 9 agent, working at the same time, rules in finem → ‘para sempre’ (one with in ætérnum and in sǽculum, D23, as Matos Soares 1932 has it in Ps 9), because ‘até o fim’ changes the sense where it is negated, and cites this verse. Douay-Rheims ‘unto the end’; Matos Soares 1932 here ‘incessantemente’. oblivísci → esquecer, direct object (glossary). The verb of the colon, ‘me esquecereis’, is the future: the psalter marks it by the accent — 12:1 obliviscéris (long ē, future) against 43:24 oblivísceris (the present, beside avértis there) — and the Greek has the future ἐπιλήσῃ. HELD AGAINST THE LATINIST’S MAJOR (draft 2), who read the present and asked for ‘me esqueceis’: he misread the form, he passed the same words on draft 1, and the blind reader heard the question as the Latin’s (‘will you forget me for good?’). The present stays with the second colon (‘desviais’, avértis), as the Latin has it.

options.label: para sempre
options.note: Ruling: the wording the Ps 9 agent proposes for the whole psalter, followed so that the two psalms, done side by side, do not diverge. ‘Até quando … para sempre?’ keeps the Latin’s own paradox (how long … to the end?). Cost: εἰς τέλος and εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα become one phrase (D15’s test would keep them apart). Heard: the blind reader took the question as ‘O Senhor me esqueceu definitivamente?’ first — the Latin’s ‘utterly’.

options.label: até o fim
options.note: Douay-Rheims: the other Greek phrase kept apart. ‘Até quando … até o fim?’ doubles ‘até’, which the Latin does not.

options.label: sem fim
options.note: Keeps the Latin’s noun (finis), apart from ‘para sempre’, with no doubled ‘até’.

decisions.why: avértere → desviar (glossary, open: ‘can serve avérte fáciem tuam’; 53:7, 118:37). A present in the Latin (the Greek has a future): ‘how long do you turn your face away from me?’. fácies → face (glossary). The same phrase in 29:8, 43:24, 50:11, 87:15; Ps 9:32 (the other agent) has ‘desviou a sua face’. Douay-Rheims ‘how long dost thou turn away thy face from me?’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘apartarás’.

options.label: desviais de mim a vossa face

forms.avertis: desviais de mim a vossa face

options.note: Ruling: the glossary verb, the Latin’s present, and ‘de mim’ moved before the object so that the verse ends on the paroxytone ‘face’.

options.label: desviais a vossa face de mim

forms.avertis: desviais a vossa face de mim

options.note: The Latin’s order; ends on the oxytone ‘mim’, as the first colon does (‘sobre mim’ ends 12:3).

options.label: afastais de mim a vossa face

forms.avertis: afastais de mim a vossa face

options.note: ‘Afastar’ is amovére / repéllere’s (glossary).

options.label: escondeis de mim a vossa face

forms.avertis: escondeis de mim a vossa face

options.note: The Diurnal’s ‘esconderás’, from the Hebrew. Refused: abscóndere is another verb (rule 1).

decisions.latin: ponam consília in ánima mea, * dolórem in corde meo
decisions.why: One verb governs both cola: ‘shall I set counsels in my soul, sorrow in my heart’ (θήσομαι βουλάς … ὀδύνας). consílium → conselho (glossary, working; open between advice and deliberation — here the soul’s own deliberations, turned over without end). ponere → pôr (Ps 11:6b ‘Porei’). Douay-Rheims ‘take counsels in my soul’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘andarei a formar projectos em minha alma’. The stylist (draft 1; his worst line): ‘“Porei conselhos” soa como uma construção transportada do latim. A imagem precisa ficar, mas “hei de pôr” dá à pergunta um movimento mais natural de queixa’. The blind reader heard ‘porei conselhos na minha alma’ first as ‘guardarei dentro de mim conselhos recebidos’ (second: ‘procurarei orientação’), and took the second colon first as ‘enquanto houver dor no coração’ — the zeugma (one verb for both objects) was not heard.

options.label: hei de pôr conselhos na minha alma

forms.consilia: hei de pôr conselhos na minha alma

options.note: Ruling (draft 2), the stylist’s: ‘haver de’ is Portuguese’s future of what one is bound to do — exactly the deliberative sense ponam can have (‘how long am I to set …?’) — and the image stays. The glossary noun is kept: the blind reader’s first hearing (advice received and kept) is not far from the Latin’s range, and ‘pôr’ makes the soul the one that sets them.

options.label: porei conselhos na minha alma
options.note: Draft 1: the Latin’s future to the letter. The stylist found it carried over from the Latin.

options.label: revolverei conselhos na minha alma
options.note: Says the turning-over the context implies; another verb, and it cannot govern ‘dor’.

options.label: porei planos na minha alma
options.note: Matos Soares 1932’s sense (‘projectos’); leaves the glossary’s ‘conselho’.

options.label: hei de pôr planos na minha alma

forms.consilia: hei de pôr planos na minha alma

options.note: Matos Soares 1932’s sense (‘projectos’): the soul’s own schemes, which ‘conselhos’ may not say to every ear; leaves the glossary word.

decisions.latin: ponam consília in ánima mea, * dolórem in corde meo
decisions.why: The Latin (and the Greek) join the two objects of ‘ponam’ without a conjunction: counsels in my soul, sorrow in my heart. The blind reader (draft 1) did not hear ‘dor’ as a second object of the verb, and took the colon as ‘enquanto houver dor no coração’.

options.label: e dor
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): ‘e’ supplied so that ‘dor’ is heard as the second thing set, as the Latin’s accusative ‘dolórem’ shows it to be; a conjunction for a case ending — grammar (D2). Matos Soares 1932 has ‘e (terei) cada dia a dor’.

options.label: dor
options.note: Draft 1: the Latin’s asyndeton. Heard by the blind reader as ‘while there is sorrow’.

decisions.why: ‘by day, through the day’ (the Greek ἡμέρας, genitive of time). Not tota die (glossary: ‘o dia todo’, 26 verses) nor per síngulos dies (‘todos os dias’). Douay-Rheims ‘all the day’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘cada dia’.

options.label: durante o dia
options.note: Ruling: per diem said as Portuguese says ‘through the day’; kept apart from tota die and per síngulos dies. Ends on a paroxytone.

options.label: cada dia
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: day after day. Near per síngulos dies (‘todos os dias’).

options.label: o dia todo
options.note: Douay-Rheims’ ‘all the day’; it is tota die’s wording (glossary, settled D24).

decisions.why: A future passive (ὑψωθήσεται) with middle sense: the enemy lifting himself above the speaker. exaltáre → exaltar (glossary); the medio-passive said with ‘se’ as Ps 7:7a exaltáre → ‘exaltai-vos’ and 8:2b ‘se elevou’. Douay-Rheims ‘be exalted over me’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘prevalecerá sobre mim’ (another verb).

options.label: se exaltará
options.note: Ruling: the pronominal form, as the glossary treats this passive elsewhere; the enemy is the one who rises. Heard: the enemy vaunting himself over me first, prevailing second.

options.label: será exaltado
options.note: The passive to the letter (Douay-Rheims); asks by whom.

decisions.why: réspice is bare; ‘me’ follows exáudi (ἐπίβλεψον, εἰσάκουσόν μου). The same Greek imperative stands behind 118:132 Áspice in me → ‘Olhai para mim’. In Ps 10:5b the verb (of the eyes, a state) became ‘estão voltados para’; at the vós imperative ‘voltai-vos’ is convértere’s (6:5), so the plain verb of looking is used. ‘Olhai’ is safe (past ‘olhei’). exáudi me → ‘escutai-me’ (D3). Douay-Rheims ‘Consider, and hear me’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘Olha para mim, e ouve-me’.

options.label: olhai
options.note: Ruling: the bare imperative for the bare imperative; the object is left to be heard from ‘escutai-me’, as in the Latin.

options.label: olhai para mim
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and 118:132’s words; supplies the object.

options.label: considerai
options.note: Douay-Rheims’ ‘Consider’; it is consideráre’s verb (glossary).

decisions.why: obdormíre: to fall asleep (the Greek ὑπνώσω); kept apart from dormíre → dormir (4:9 dórmiam) and dormitáre → dormitar (118:28). The other place is 43:23 Exsúrge, quare obdórmis, Dómine? (grep). ‘ne umquam’ → ‘para que nunca’; the Latin varies it to ‘nequándo’ in the next colon (the Greek has μήποτε both times), and Portuguese keeps the variation at no cost (glossary nequándo → ‘para que não’). Douay-Rheims ‘that I never sleep in death’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘para que eu nunca durma na morte’.

options.label: adormeça
options.note: Ruling: the ingressive verb for the ingressive verb — to fall asleep in death, the moment and not the state. Heard: ‘morra fisicamente’ first, spiritual death second — as the Latin.

options.label: durma
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and Douay-Rheims: dormíre’s verb (glossary).

decisions.why: A future perfect passive of movére (σαλευθῶ, ‘be shaken’): if I am moved, shaken. The same verb in the confident ‘Non movébor’ (9:27, 29:7, 61:3 — grep). Douay-Rheims ‘when I am moved’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘se eu for abalado’.

options.label: se eu for abalado
options.note: Ruling: Matos Soares 1932; ‘abalar’ is the shaking the Greek names and serves ‘não serei abalado’ (Non movébor).

options.label: se eu vacilar
options.note: Active and plain; loses the passive and the outside force.

options.label: se eu cair
options.note: The Diurnal’s ‘porque eu caia’. Another verb (cádere).

decisions.latin: cantábo Dómino qui bona tríbuit mihi
decisions.why: tríbuere: to allot, bestow (15:7 qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum; 27:4 tríbue illis; 36:21 — grep); the Greek has one word, τῷ εὐεργετήσαντί με, ‘who did me good’. bona (neuter plural) is ‘good things’. Douay-Rheims ‘who giveth me good things’; Matos Soares 1932 ‘que me deu bens’. The stylist (draft 1): ‘“Concedeu bens” tem uma secura administrativa e sugere sobretudo patrimônio’ → ‘que me deu coisas boas’. The blind reader heard ‘me concedeu bens’ first as ‘deu-me posses ou recursos materiais’.

options.label: que me deu coisas boas
options.note: Ruling (draft 2), the stylist’s: ‘coisas boas’ is bona as a hearer takes it (good things of any kind — which is what the Greek εὐεργετήσαντι, ‘who did me good’, says too), and ‘dar’ is the plain verb; tríbuere and dare never meet in a verse (15:7 qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum will read ‘que me deu entendimento’). The colon ends on a paroxytone. Tested (draft 2): the blind reader raised no item on the colon.

options.label: que me concedeu bens
options.note: Draft 1. ‘Bens’ was heard by the blind reader as property first; the stylist found ‘concedeu bens’ administrative.

options.label: que me deu bens
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the plainer verb, which is dare’s.

options.label: que me fez bem
options.note: The Greek’s sense. Refused: the Latin has a verb of giving and an object (rule 1).

decisions.why: 7:18b word for word; D25 settles psállere → entoar salmos and says that 12:6b copies Ps 7’s colon. Here the colon stands beside cantábo (12:6b’s middle colon), which is why psállere cannot be ‘cantar’ (D25).

options.label: e entoarei salmos ao nome do altíssimo Senhor

forms.psallam: e entoarei salmos ao nome do altíssimo Senhor

options.note: Ruling: Ps 7:18b copied word for word (D25, glossary formula).

options.label: e entoarei salmos ao nome do Senhor altíssimo

forms.psallam: e entoarei salmos ao nome do Senhor altíssimo

options.note: Matos Soares 1932’s order (the same words); the verse would end on a proparoxytone, which is why Ps 7 moved the adjective.

options.label: e cantarei salmos ao nome do altíssimo Senhor

forms.psallam: e cantarei salmos ao nome do altíssimo Senhor

options.note: Refused by D25: ‘cantarei … cantarei’ in this very verse would make two Latin verbs one.

choices.12:1: The psalm begins at 12:1: DO puts the titulus (In finem, Psalmus David) outside the verse, and 12:1 is the first prayed verse (D7). ‘Senhor’ bare (glossary).
choices.12:2: The Latin’s question mark kept. ‘dor’ (dolor, glossary) is the second object of ‘hei de pôr’, as dolórem of ponam; ‘e’ supplied (decision zeugma).
choices.12:3: The inline marker (4a) is not reproduced. exáudi me → ‘escutai-me’ (D3; the imperative is safe). Dómine, Deus meus → ‘Senhor, meu Deus’ (glossary formula). The imperative begins with a lower-case letter after the mark, as the Latin’s.
choices.12:4b: illumináre → iluminar (glossary; ‘Iluminai’ is safe, past ‘iluminei’). nequándo → ‘para que não’ (glossary, 2:12). præválere advérsus → ‘prevalecer contra’ (Matos Soares 1932 ‘Prevaleci contra ele’); the enemy’s words are quoted with a capital, as the Latin. The inline marker (5a) is not reproduced.
choices.12:5b: tribuláre → atribular (glossary, Ps 3:2 ‘os que me atribulam’). exsultáre → exultar. ego autem → ‘mas eu’ (5:7b, 118:69); speráre in → esperar em (glossary), the perfect kept (‘esperei’, as 7:2 ‘em vós esperei’). The inline marker (6a) is not reproduced. The blind reader listed ‘atribulam’ as unknown (as in Ps 3); kept (glossary).
choices.12:6b: salutáre → salvação (D6); ‘exultará na vossa salvação’ as Ps 9:16a (the other agent) ‘Exultarei na vossa salvação’. cantáre → cantar (D25 keeps it apart from psállere).

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm12.txt, six prayed verses with DO’s ids (12:1, 12:2, 12:3, 12:4b, 12:5b, 12:6b; the inline markers (4a), (5a), (6a) are not reproduced). 12:6b has a flex and a mediant; every other verse one ‘*’. Douay-Rheims from Bolls’ chapter 13 (= Vulgate Ps 12, checked by the coordinator).

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps012.md. Sense from the Vulgate family (Douay-Rheims; Matos Soares 1932 by its text layer). The Diurnal Monástico 1962 has the psalm, made from the Hebrew: diction only (12:1 ‘esconderás’, 12:5b ‘caia’ refused as the Hebrew’s). DO’s Portuguese not used (D12). Repeats found with ps005/grep_latin.py and ps010/grep_done.py: 12:6b last colon = 7:18b (copied, D25); in finem (19 lines; the Ps 9 agent’s ruling followed); avértis fáciem tuam a me (29:8, 43:24, 87:15); obdormíre 43:23; movére (Non movébor 9:27, 29:7, 61:3); tríbuere 15:7, 27:4; quámdiu 103:33, 145:2a (another use); in salutári tuo 9:16a, 19:6. Vós imperatives: ‘olhai’, ‘escutai-me’, ‘Iluminai’ — all safe. Septuagintal readings kept against the Hebrew: 12:2 per diem as ‘by day’; 12:3 réspice (look); 12:6b the Latin’s longer ending with psallam (the Hebrew has no third colon).

Draft 1: hard pass. Soft flags, accepted: 12:3 second colon −4 (the Latin’s vocative ‘Dómine, Deus meus’ is two words in Portuguese); 12:5b +3 / −3 (‘os que me atribulam’; ‘mas eu’); 12:6b last colon +5 — the Ps 7:18b colon copied word for word (D25), whose length was accepted there. Every cadence is oxytone or paroxytone; no rhyme flag.

Draft 1: clean — ‘Não encontrei falhas de adequação: a tradução preserva os sentidos, as imagens e as relações gramaticais do latim. Todos os versículos mantêm as mesmas marcas de divisão, na mesma ordem.’ Passed without remark: ‘Até quando’ four times (quámdiu merged), ‘para sempre’ for in finem, ‘desviais de mim a vossa face’, ‘porei conselhos’, ‘durante o dia’, ‘se exaltará’, bare ‘olhai’, ‘adormeça’, ‘se eu for abalado’, the copied 7:18b colon.

Draft 1. Two verses; best 12:3, worst 12:2. ‘O salmo tem sobriedade e uma insistência orante bem sustentada pelos repetidos “Até quando”. As terminações atendem à cadência pedida, sem rimas salientes.’ Both taken.

outcomes.remark: ‘porei conselhos’ sounds carried over from the Latin → ‘Até quando hei de pôr conselhos na minha alma’
outcomes.reason: A periphrastic future for the future (or deliberative subjunctive) ponam: how it is said, not what (D2); the image stays.

outcomes.remark: ‘concedeu bens’ is administrative and suggests property → ‘que me deu coisas boas’
outcomes.reason: The blind reader heard property too; ‘coisas boas’ is bona.

audit.note: Draft 1, Portuguese only. Eleven items, one unknown word (atribulam). Two real faults, both mended in draft 2: 12:2 the zeugma not heard (‘enquanto houver dor’), 12:6b ‘bens’ heard as property. The rest is the Latin’s own range.

outcomes.remark: ‘me esquecereis para sempre?’: how long will it last / forgotten me for good (heard first)
‘desviais de mim a vossa face’: turn the face / withdraw attention and help (heard first)
‘porei conselhos na minha alma’: keep advice received (heard first) / seek guidance within
outcomes.reason: Kept (glossary noun) under the stylist’s ‘hei de pôr’; ‘planos’ added as an option.

outcomes.remark: ‘… na minha alma, dor no meu coração’: set both / while there is sorrow (heard first)
outcomes.reason: A misparse the Latin’s accusative excludes; ‘e’ supplied.

outcomes.remark: ‘se exaltará sobre mim’: vaunt himself (heard first) / prevail
‘Iluminai os meus olhos’: give light or strength to the eyes / make me see spiritually (heard first)
‘adormeça na morte’: die (heard first) / spiritual death
‘se eu for abalado’: shaken in spirit (heard first) / defeated
‘esperei na vossa misericórdia’: trusted (heard first) / waited
outcomes.reason: speráre in → esperar em (glossary), heard as trust.

outcomes.remark: ‘na vossa salvação’: deliverance / spiritual salvation (heard first)
‘me concedeu bens’: possessions (heard first) / good things

outcomes.reason: Glossary (tribuláre → atribular, Ps 3:2), listed as unknown there too.

audit.note: v2. Two verses changed against draft 1: 12:2 ‘Até quando hei de pôr conselhos na minha alma, * e dor no meu coração durante o dia?’ (the stylist’s ‘hei de pôr’; ‘e’ for the zeugma the blind reader missed); 12:6b ‘cantarei ao Senhor, que me deu coisas boas’ (the stylist’s; ‘bens’ was heard as property). Draft 1 is prayed.v1.json (flat text prayed.v1.vos.json, the file the three v1 critics read).

Draft 2: hard pass. Soft flags as draft 1: 12:3 second colon −4, 12:5b +3 / −3, 12:6b last colon +5 (the copied 7:18b colon). 12:2 first colon grows by ‘hei de’; every cadence oxytone or paroxytone; no rhyme flag.

Draft 2 — the gate. NOT clean: one major, held on purpose (12:1). ‘obliviscéris me’ read as a present → ‘me esqueceis’. The accented form is the future (43:24 has the present oblivísceris), the Greek is future, and he passed the same words on draft 1. Nothing else: the two draft-2 changes (12:2 ‘hei de pôr … e dor’, 12:6b ‘que me deu coisas boas’) passed, and all division marks are in the Latin’s order.

outcomes.remark: ‘me esquecereis’ puts the present obliviscéris in the future → ‘me esqueceis’ (MAJOR)
outcomes.reason: A misreading: obliviscéris (accent on -scé-, long ē) is the future; the present is 43:24 oblivísceris. Greek ἐπιλήσῃ, future. He passed it on draft 1 (D24: weighed, not obeyed).

audit.note: Draft 2, Portuguese only — run to test the two fixes. Both hold: 12:2 ‘e dor no meu coração’ is heard as a second object of ‘pôr’ (setting sorrow / carrying it — both the Latin’s), no longer as ‘while there is sorrow’; 12:6b ‘que me deu coisas boas’ drew no item. Unknown words: atribulam (again), exultarão, exultará (glossary: exsultáre → exultar, listed as unknown before and kept). The rest is the Latin’s own range, as draft 1.

outcomes.remark: ‘e dor no meu coração’: set sorrow in one’s own heart / carry sorrow (heard first)
outcomes.reason: The fix holds; both readings are ponam … dolórem.

outcomes.remark: ‘pôr conselhos na minha alma’: keep advice received (heard first) / deliberate
